title: Ahrens Moving Average (AHRENS)
summary: A recursive average that steps toward price from the midpoint of its previous value and its value one period ago.
descriptionHtml:
The Ahrens Moving Average updates itself from its own history. On each bar it takes the midpoint of its previous value and its value Period bars ago, measures how far the source sits from that midpoint, and moves its previous value by that distance divided by Period.

Using the midpoint of two of its own past values, rather than the previous value alone, corrects some of the lag a plain recursive average builds up. On the first bar the line starts at the source, and until it has a value Period bars back the source stands in for that older value.
howToReadHtml:
Read it as a smooth trend line. Price above a rising line describes an uptrend and price below a falling line a downtrend; the slope of the line shows the direction of the trend and how firmly it is holding.

The line moves only 1 / Period of the gap each bar, so it is slow to respond to a sudden move and can trail price for some time after a sharp break. A shorter period makes it follow more closely at the cost of more noise.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How far back the older value is taken and how small each step is. Longer is smoother and slower.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series the average follows, the close by default.

faq.q: Why does it use its own value from a period ago?
faq.html: The midpoint of the previous value and the value a period back sits closer to the centre of recent movement, which offsets some of the lag of stepping from the previous value alone.
No. It starts at the source on the first bar, but the first Period bars use the source in place of the older value, so they settle in over that stretch.

related.title: Arnaud Legoux Moving Average (ALMA)
related.summary: A Gaussian-weighted moving average whose peak weight can slide from the middle of the window toward the newest bar.

related.title: ADX Variable Moving Average (ADXVMA)
related.summary: An adaptive average that uses the ADX as its smoothing factor, following price closely in a strong trend and flattening in a range.

related.title: Blackman Moving Average (BLMA)
related.summary: A moving average weighted by the Blackman window, a three-term cosine taper that falls to zero at both ends of the lookback.
